name: BFGS inverse-Hessian update
definition: Given s=x_(k+1)−x_k, y=∇f(x_(k+1))−∇f(x_k), ρ=1/(yᵀs), update H_(k+1)=(I−ρsyᵀ)H_k(I−ρysᵀ)+ρssᵀ; choose direction d_k=−H_k∇f(x_k).
variables: f differentiable objective; H positive-definite inverse-Hessian approximation; s displacement; y gradient change; ρ reciprocal curvature
assumptions: Smooth objective, positive-definite starting approximation, positive curvature yᵀs>0; safeguarded line search for convergence.
limitations: Dense storage and updates scale quadratically; noisy gradients or nonconvex curvature can invalidate the update.
computation: Calculate gradient difference and rank-two inverse-Hessian update; use a suitable line search and stop rule.

source.citation: Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., chapter 6; SciPy BFGS documentation. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/optimize.minimize-bfgs.html

name: Gauss–Newton nonlinear least squares
definition: For f(x)=0.5||r(x)||₂² with residual Jacobian J, choose d_k=argmin_d ||J(x_k)d+r(x_k)||₂² and update x_(k+1)=x_k+α_k d_k.
variables: r residual vector; J residual Jacobian; d linearized least-squares step; α step length
assumptions: Differentiable residuals, a well-conditioned full-column-rank Jacobian for unique unregularized step, suitable initialization and globalization.
limitations: Neglects residual-weighted second derivatives; large residuals or singular Jacobians can lead to unreliable steps.
failure_conditions: Rank deficiency or failed descent without an appropriate safeguard
computation: Solve the linearized least-squares problem with QR or SVD, then apply a safeguarded step.

source.citation: Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., chapter 10, Gauss–Newton method.

name: Levenberg–Marquardt damped least-squares step
definition: For f(x)=0.5||r(x)||₂² choose d solving (JᵀJ+λI)d=−Jᵀr, λ>0; update x only when a prespecified actual-versus-model reduction safeguard accepts the step.
variables: r residual vector; J residual Jacobian; λ positive damping; d damped direction
assumptions: Differentiable residuals, finite quantities, adaptive damping and convergence criteria specified; positive λ makes the stated system positive definite in exact arithmetic.
limitations: Damping and scaling affect convergence; may stall at poor local minima; stated isotropic damping is one convention.
failure_conditions: Nonfinite Jacobian, inconsistent scaling or absent damping acceptance policy
computation: Solve the damped least-squares system, preferably as augmented least squares, and adjust damping using the accepted reduction policy.

source.citation: Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., chapter 10; SciPy nonlinear least-squares documentation. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.optimize.least_squares.html

application: General regularized step for nonlinear residual fitting on authorised development records.

mechanism_note: Positive damping changes the linearized subproblem and step control, not just its solver.

name: Cyclic exact coordinate minimization
definition: For coordinate j_k=1+(k mod d), choose t_k∈argmin_t f(x_k+t e_(j_k)), then x_(k+1)=x_k+t_k e_(j_k).
variables: f objective; d dimension; e_j coordinate unit vector; t exact scalar minimizer
assumptions: Each coordinate subproblem has an attained minimizer; cyclic coverage; convergence requires additional objective regularity and boundedness conditions.
limitations: May progress slowly along strongly coupled coordinates; nonconvex or nonsmooth objectives need specific convergence analysis.
failure_conditions: Unbounded coordinate subproblem or nonattained minimum
computation: Solve each scalar coordinate subproblem in cyclic order, specify ties and stopping criteria.

name: Trust-region dogleg step
definition: For positive-definite B, g≠0 and radius Δ>0, let p_U=−(gᵀg)/(gᵀBg) g and p_B=−B^(−1)g. If ||p_B||≤Δ use p_B; if ||p_U||≥Δ use −Δg/||g||; otherwise choose p=p_U+τ(p_B−p_U), τ∈(0,1), ||p||=Δ.
variables: g gradient; B positive-definite model Hessian; Δ radius; p_U unconstrained Cauchy-line minimizer; p_B Newton step
assumptions: Positive-definite quadratic model and positive trust radius; actual/predicted reduction acceptance and radius policy for iterative algorithm.
limitations: Positive-definite model required for standard dogleg; approximate rather than exact general trust-region solution.
computation: Compute both directions, check boundary cases, solve scalar quadratic for segment intersection and apply a documented trust-region update.

source.citation: Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., chapter 4, dogleg method. https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/optimize.minimize-dogleg.html

name: Armijo backtracking line search
definition: Given gᵀd<0, α_0>0, β∈(0,1), c∈(0,1), choose smallest j≥0 satisfying f(x+α_0β^j d)≤f(x)+c α_0β^j gᵀd; set α=α_0β^j.
variables: f objective; x current point; g gradient; d descent direction; α trial length; β contraction; c sufficient-decrease constant
assumptions: Differentiability near x and strict descent direction for finite termination in exact arithmetic; finite feasible trial evaluations.
limitations: Only sufficient decrease, not curvature control; very small accepted steps or numerical precision may impede progress.
failure_conditions: Non-descent direction or nonfinite evaluations without a safe trial limit
computation: Evaluate geometric trial lengths until the Armijo inequality holds, otherwise report failure at a prespecified bound.

source.citation: Nocedal and Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed., chapter 3, backtracking line search and sufficient decrease.
